prompt: The movement of people from agricultural areas to cities can cause serious problems in both places. What are the serious problems? What measures can be used to solve these problems?
essay:
The relocation of citizens from rural to urban areas may result in grave issues , including the increasing of traffic volume and housing prices in the cities. However, regulating accommodations' costs by the state and building an efficient transportation system are two viable solutions.

Having individuals move from the countryside to the city will cause more traffic. Since urban zones are usually crowded, they have residents. Therefore, by welcoming more people, the traffic density will intensify subsequently, which will detrimentally affect the environment by releasing more toxic emissions into the atmosphere. Moreover, this will also increase the prices of living spaces, because of the high demand from the newcomers, thus, landlords will raise their prices, which will even impact the locals. For instance, in search of jobs, many Saudis from all around the country move to Riyadh , which has caused a surge in the cost of living spaces in the city.

The government can assess these challenges. First, it can control the prices of housing using the regulatory tools, by implementing laws against any unfair practises such as placing a limit on meter prices when selling living accommodations by real estate developers, or implementing taxes on landlords that increase accordingly with the prices of their rental units. Furthermore, the state can also build a public transportation system that is affordable and convenient , which could decrease the traffic flow since it will offer people  alternative methods of transportation rather than riding personal cars. For example, many capitals around the world , such as Riyadh, London, Paris and Tokyo, have efficient underground systems that serve the growing population of these cities.

In conclusion, although the movement of citizens from farming zones to cities has resulted in higher traffic rates and  higher housing costs, the government can confront these challenges by enforcing laws that control the accommodation prices and build an efficient public transportation system.
